quizzes.title: Wild Things
quizzes.description: Giants, speedsters and curious creatures from around the animal kingdom.

questions.q: What is the largest animal alive today?
questions.note: Blue whales can grow to around 30 metres long.

questions.q: Which animal is called the 'ship of the desert'?
questions.note: Camels can go days without water and cross soft sand on wide, padded feet.

questions.q: A spider is a type of insect.
questions.note: Spiders are arachnids: they have eight legs, while insects have six.

questions.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.note: A newborn joey is about the size of a jelly bean.

questions.q: Which is the only mammal that can truly fly?
questions.note: Flying squirrels, sugar gliders and colugos only glide; bats flap their wings.

questions.q: Which is the tallest animal in the world?
questions.note: Despite its long neck, a giraffe has seven neck bones, the same as humans.

questions.q: Dolphins are mammals.
questions.note: Dolphins breathe air and feed their young on milk.

questions.q: What is a group of lions called?
questions.note: Lions are the only big cats that regularly live in groups.

questions.q: Which black-and-white bear from China eats mostly bamboo?
questions.note: Accept "panda"; a giant panda can spend over half the day eating.

questions.q: What is the largest living bird?
questions.note: Ostriches can't fly, but they lay the largest eggs of any living bird.

quizzes.title: Flower Power
quizzes.description: How plants eat, drink, breathe and grow.

questions.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air for photosynthesis?
questions.note: Plants combine carbon dioxide and water, using sunlight, to make sugar.

questions.q: Plants release oxygen during photosynthesis.
questions.note: Much of the oxygen we breathe was made by plants and ocean algae.

questions.q: What green pigment lets plants capture energy from sunlight?
questions.note: Leaves change colour in autumn as chlorophyll breaks down.

questions.q: Which part of a plant takes up water and anchors it in the soil?
questions.note: Accept "root".

questions.q: What are the tiny pores on a leaf that let gases in and out called?
questions.note: Stomata can open and close to control how much water the plant loses.

questions.q: What sugary liquid do bees collect from flowers to make honey?
questions.note: Bees also carry pollen between flowers, which helps plants reproduce.

questions.q: Mushrooms are a type of plant.
questions.note: Mushrooms are fungi, a separate kingdom of life from plants.

questions.q: Which part of a flower develops into the fruit?
questions.note: That's why tomatoes and cucumbers count as fruits to a botanist.

questions.q: What is the loss of water vapour from a plant's leaves called?
questions.note: Transpiration helps pull water up from the roots to the leaves.

questions.q: What kind of plant is a Venus flytrap?
questions.note: Its trap snaps shut when trigger hairs inside are touched twice in quick succession.

quizzes.title: Wild Weather
quizzes.description: Clouds, storms and the instruments that help us forecast them.

questions.q: Which instrument measures air pressure?
questions.note: Falling air pressure often means stormy weather is on the way.

questions.q: A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
questions.note: Lightning can reach about 27,000 °C, roughly five times hotter than the Sun's surface.

questions.q: What is a hurricane called when it forms in the northwest Pacific Ocean?
questions.note: In the Indian Ocean and around Australia, the same storms are called cyclones.

questions.q: What instrument measures wind speed?
questions.note: Most anemometers use spinning cups that turn faster as the wind picks up.

questions.q: Which tall, towering type of cloud produces thunderstorms?
questions.note: Cumulonimbus clouds can tower more than 10 km into the sky.

questions.q: Which scale rates tornadoes by the damage they cause?
questions.note: It is named after Japanese-American meteorologist Ted Fujita.

questions.q: Snowflakes usually have eight sides or points.
questions.note: Snowflakes have six sides because of the way water molecules bond as they freeze.

questions.q: What is the calm centre of a hurricane called?
questions.note: The strongest winds swirl in the eyewall that surrounds the eye.

questions.q: What are the balls of ice that fall from thunderstorm clouds called?
questions.note: Accept "hailstones".

questions.q: Which colour is on the outer edge of a primary rainbow?
questions.note: Violet sits on the inside edge of the arc.

quizzes.title: Planet Earth Explorer
quizzes.description: Reefs, deserts, forests and the science of how ecosystems work.

questions.q: What is the world's largest coral reef system?
questions.note: It lies off the coast of Queensland, Australia, and can be seen from space.

questions.q: Most of the Amazon rainforest lies within Brazil.
questions.note: Around 60% of the Amazon is in Brazil, with the rest spread across eight other countries and territories.

questions.q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.note: Counting cold deserts too, Antarctica is the largest desert of all.

questions.q: What word describes a species found naturally in only one place on Earth?
questions.note: Lemurs, for example, are endemic to Madagascar.

questions.q: What is ground that stays frozen all year round called?
questions.note: Permafrost can store huge amounts of carbon that is released as it thaws.

questions.q: What is another name for the boreal forest?
questions.note: The taiga stretches across Canada, Scandinavia and Russia.

questions.q: Coral is a type of plant.
questions.note: Corals are animals, related to jellyfish and sea anemones.

questions.q: What is the term for a species' role and position within its ecosystem?
questions.note: Two species competing for exactly the same niche rarely coexist for long.

questions.q: What is the name of the deepest known point in the ocean, in the Mariana Trench?
questions.note: It is nearly 11 km deep, deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

questions.q: What process turns nitrogen gas from the air into a form plants can use?
questions.note: Bacteria in the root nodules of peas and beans are famous nitrogen fixers.
